comparator.sourceNotes: The current programme-specific regulations account for the full 180 EC: 60 EC compulsory in year one; 45 EC fixed sociology and methods, one 5-EC field course and its corresponding 10-EC project in year two; and a 30-EC broadening minor, 25 EC fixed work and one different 5-EC field course in year three. The normalized registry target names the general bachelor and supplies no student-specific field preference. The route therefore uses the first listed year-two field course (Social Networks), its required corresponding project, and then the first listed year-three field course not already taken (Labour Sociology), before considering UCR fit. The 30-EC broadening minor remains genuine approved choice space. The official current bachelor page independently confirms the 180-EC duration, field-specialisation structure and live curriculum.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target does not name one of the four field specialisations. The formal 2026–2027 regulations list Social Networks first for the year-two choose-one set and require the project to correspond, so Social Networks and Project Social Networks are selected. Year three requires one field course not already taken; Labour Sociology is the first remaining item in the same official list. This neutral source-order decision was made before assessing UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three sociology-led options are supported. They focus on broad social inquiry, work and organisations, and public safety. Each pair differs by at least 8 courses in each direction. The public safety option centres on institutions and social risks without promising specialist digital-crime study.

notes.text: Groningen builds a sociology sequence with four statistics courses, two qualitative-methods courses, field projects and a compulsory thesis. UCR covers related theory and methods across disciplines. Its optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a broadening minor. Students choose university minors or seek approval for a personal minor outside Sociology.

audience.programmeDescription: Sociology at the University of Groningen examines how people, groups and institutions shape society. Students study theory and research methods, carry out field projects and complete a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options combine sociology and social research in three options focused on inequality and public issues, work and organisations, or crime and public safety.

componentNotes.y2-neighbourhood-project: Pass at least two of the three first-year statistics courses before starting this project.
componentNotes.y2-social-networks: This field course is paired with the Social Networks project.
componentNotes.y2-network-project: Take the project that matches the selected field course.
componentNotes.y3-labour-sociology: The third-year field must differ from the second-year field.
componentNotes.y3-minor: Choose 30 EC outside Sociology under the broadening-minor rules.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Complete all first-year courses and all projects before starting the thesis.
